Subject: Procurement questionnaire — uptime/latency verification

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to gather a short, concrete packet on how Redwood measures the SLA items (uptime and P95 latency) so we can move the contract forward. The checklist they provided is fairly prescriptive — a few clarifying questions below so we don't chase the wrong artifacts: 

1) For uptime: do you calculate from successful API responses (2xx) over a rolling 30-day window, or a different window/definition?
2) For latency: is the P95 computed on ingress-to-last-token-emitted, and do you exclude outlier maintenance windows?
3) Sampling: do you sample 100% of production traffic for measurement, or do you use a statistical sampling approach? If sampled, what's the sample size and confidence interval?
4) Can you provide an export (dashboard or CSV) showing one representative 30-day measurement and the alerts fired in that window?
5) We may need temporary, read-only dashboard access for our SRE to validate — what's the process and typical turnaround?

We'd like the packet by EOD Friday if possible. I'm looping Amit (vendor approvals) and procurement so they see the ask.

Best,
Julia Park
Senior IT Procurement
CloudSoft

Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — uptime/latency verification

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers and I'll attach the sample artifacts you requested. Marcus and Karthik are cc'd for backup on instrumentation details.

1) Uptime definition: we compute availability as percentage of successful API responses (2xx) over a rolling 30-day window by default. Internal logs also maintain 1-day and 90-day windows for trend analysis. Planned maintenance windows that were communicated via the Console update are excluded from contractual availability calculations if scheduled >72 hours in advance.

2) Latency (P95): measured as time from request acceptance at the edge to last-token-emitted for streaming calls, and to response complete for non-streaming. P95 is computed on the same rolling 30-day window as uptime. We exclude maintenance windows and recognized downstream dependency outages from the contractual P95 calculation; all exclusions are documented in the incident and audit logs.

3) Sampling: we perform full sampling (100%) for control-plane SLA metrics for hosted customers on production. For very high-volume customers on Dedicated, we may apply stratified sampling for long-tail analysis; we'll flag if sampling is in effect and provide confidence intervals. For CloudSoft (hosted plan), measurements are full-fidelity.

4) Export: attached are two artifacts — the measurement spec PDF (redwood-slo-measurement-spec-2026-10.pdf) and a Grafana JSON export for a representative 30-day window (grafana-sample-export-2026-09-30.json). The export includes P95 and availability series and the alert firing timeline.

5) Dashboard access: we can grant a read-only, time-limited Grafana view for a named SRE (SAML-based SSO). Typical turnaround: 48 business hours after the signed NDA/PO. For procurement evaluation only we can also provide a limited Shared Snapshot link within 24 hours that contains the same panels but is immutable.

If you need precise CSV tables for ingestion into procurement systems, tell me the columns you want and we can export them.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Lead, Customer Reliability & Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Hi Amit / Julia — Marcus here, ops. Short answers and next steps below.

1) Temporary dashboard access: we can grant Martin a read-only SAML account for 72 hours. Please have your SSO admin send an access request email to security-access@redwood.com with the username and HR contact. Once we receive the request and the minimal NDAs are in place (we can accept the procurement questionnaire signed), turnaround is typically 24–48 hours.

2) Exception / carveout for customer-driven migrations: yes — we support a formal "scheduled-impact" carveout. Process: customer submits a Scheduled Impact Request (SIR) via our Console (Support > Scheduled Events) at least 7 days before the event and selects the desired carveout window. Maximum standard carveout is 8 hours per event; for one-time multi-hour migrations we can extend to 24 hours with advance notice and an operational runbook (we require at least one Redwood engineer on-call during the window). All carveouts are recorded and excluded from the contractual availability/latency calculations for the agreed period.

I've added a short checklist you can follow before submitting the SIR:
- Provide event start/end in UTC and expected QPS delta
- Submit an ops runbook and rollback plan
- Designate a Redwood point-of-contact (we'll propose one when you submit the SIR)

I'll open an internal support ticket and pre-stage the read-only Grafana snapshot. Link to the pre-staged dashboard (read-only snapshot): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/customer-cloudsoft-dashboard?orgId=1.

If you'd like I can also schedule a 30-min handover meeting with our on-call engineer to walk Martin through panels and the alert rules — propose times and we'll work it in.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference
